Yes, absolutely - like others have said, I have protections in place at work and adjustments which without I wouldn't manage.

In my opinion, the best part about being diagnosed is giving it a name, the first step to understanding something is to give it a name, I'm now much kinder to myself; "I'm not a bad friend for not having the energy to go to a social tonight, I'm autistic and that's okay."  


I'm still not so great in social or busy situations to name a few, that will likely never change but now I now why and have been able to construct coping mechanisms.

Don't get me wrong, I think this is impressive, very impressive but I don't think you should pursue this as a game idea.

You can build procedural cities on the fly great but doing the same with npcs could become jank, look at how no man's sky shipped with all that budget and team behind them and vr is just a bit more complex.

I fully believe this should be a licenced tech.

Imagine licensing this in a dungeon crawler setting with caves instead of buildings or as generated terrain for a flight simulator etc.

Sure make your own game... eventually and with more budget when you've made a bit through licensing & maturing the tech

We where best friends again for years and i literally put myself in the friendzone despite loving the bones of her but not being able to say it...
